text:
### Observed differences

- Two groups of activities exchanged their place in the trace. In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 appeared in every trace at a mean relative position of about 0.64, while A19, A21 and A24 appeared in roughly 3 in 10 traces at about 0.36; in the later window, A20/A22/A23 sit at about 0.38 and A19/A21/A24 at about 0.67, with participation essentially unchanged on both sides. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- The handover after each block swapped: in the earlier window, A19, A21 and A24 led almost exclusively to A25 (about 93–97 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions) and A20/A22/A23 led to A30 in about 29–37 in 100 of theirs; in the later window, A19/A21/A24 lead almost exclusively to A30 (about 92–97 in 100) and A20/A22/A23 lead to A25 in about 28–37 in 100, while the succession among A20, A22 and A23 themselves is preserved. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011]
- Pair-level evidence matches: A22→A30 and A23→A30 within five steps fell from about 199–200 in 200 traces to 1 in 200, while A19→A30, A21→A30, A22→A25, A23→A25, A29→A21 and A40→A22 rose from about 1 in 200 traces to 58–200 in 200, typically one to three steps apart; A21→A25 and A40→A21, previously one step apart in about 94–97 in 100 of the traces containing them, nearly disappeared, and the gap from A29 to A30 shortened from about four steps to about two. [LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG023, LAG024, LAG025, LAG026, LAG027, LAG028]
- A29 and A40, which precede this segment, now lead into the opposite group: A29's outgoing transitions went from mostly A20, A23 and A22 (about 37/33/29 in 100) to mostly A24, A19 and A21 (about 38/32/28 in 100), and A40's went from mostly A21, A24 and A19 to mostly A22, A20 and A23. [DIR012, DIR013]
- A08 became much rarer and lost its tight link to A16: it appeared in about 64 in 100 traces in the earlier window versus about 29 in 100 in the later one (127 vs 57 of 200), its mean relative position moved later (about 0.26 to 0.41), and its transitions to A16 fell from about 93 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions to about 31 in 100, with the A08→A16 pair one step apart dropping from about 99 in 100 to about 43 in 100. [OCC003, POS001, DIR002, LAG001]
- A04, A06 and A10 appeared roughly three times as often: trace participation rose from about 7% to 21% for A04, about 7% to 24% for A06 and about 9% to 19% for A10, with redirected successors (for example A10 now often continues to A46 or A15); the earlier window contains only 13–17 traces with each of these activities, so these estimates rest on few cases. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]
- Smaller shifts: A15 now continues to A16 in about 88 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 61 in the earlier window) and to A08 in about 7 (about 39 earlier); A14→A15 weakened from about 97 to about 80 in 100; A45→A46 is now two steps apart in about 16 in 100 of cases (about 2 earlier). [DIR004, DIR005, LAG030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two blocks of activities exchanged their relative order: the block A20, A22, A23 — previously executed late in each trace (mean relative position about 0.64, in every trace in both windows) — now runs early (about 0.38), while A19, A21 and A24 moved from about 0.36 to about 0.67 with stable participation (about 3 in 10 traces in both windows). As part of the same difference, A25 — previously the near-exclusive immediate successor of A19/A21/A24 — now follows A20/A22/A23, A30 — previously a frequent successor of A20/A22/A23 — now immediately follows A19/A21/A24, and A29 and A40 now lead into the opposite group than before. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]

This hypothesis is shown directly and consistently: the positional shifts occur on activities present in 100% of traces in both windows, the successor replacements are near-complete on three source activities each, and the within-five-step pair frequencies flip between about 200 and 1 out of 200 traces in both directions; in total 58 items qualified against fewer than 1 expected for an unchanged process, and each item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits, so chance sampling cannot account for the ensemble. [LAG018, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG023, LAG024]

The evidence cannot fully rule out that the two windows sample a different mix of trace variants — for example both orders already existed and their shares shifted — rather than a reordering applied within comparable traces; the exchange is also documented only on the roughly 3-in-10 traces containing A19, A21 or A24, and positions and gaps are measured in event steps, not clock time. [POS002, POS004, POS007, LAG018, LAG019]

Other differences: A08 became far less frequent (about 64% vs 29% of traces) and its link to A16 loosened; A04, A06 and A10 became roughly three times as common with redirected successors (weak before-support); A15 now usually continues to A16 rather than to A08, and A45→A46 is sometimes two steps apart. [OCC003, DIR002, OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR005, LAG030]
